name: Volume clock variance ratio
note: Two resamplings of the same tape: the bars as they come (clock time) and the same volume repacked into equal-volume buckets of size V = the trailing median bar volume, splitting any bar that overfills a bucket pro rata and interpolating its close linearly to the split point. Q = RV_clock / RV_vol over a rolling window, percentile-ranked against its own trailing history. A high Q means price is travelling per unit of clock time far more than per unit of volume - moving without participation - so the last look bars' move is faded; below the low percentile nothing is taken. Built and traded inside the regular session only, because an extended-hours bar's few hundred shares make the bucket size meaningless.
source: Motivated by Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara, 'The Volume Clock: Insights into the High Frequency Paradigm', Journal of Portfolio Management 39(1), 2012 (SSRN 2034858). I attempted to fetch the SSRN page and received HTTP 403, so this is a bibliographic citation, not a verified quotation; the RV_clock / RV_vol ratio and the trading rule are my synthesis.
code:
_TT = [0, 3, 2, 5, 0, 3, 5, 1, 4, 6, 2, 4]


def _nth_sunday(y, mo, n):
    yy = y - (1 if mo < 3 else 0)
    d1 = (yy + yy // 4 - yy // 100 + yy // 400 + _TT[mo - 1] + 1) % 7
    return 1 + ((7 - d1) % 7) + 7 * (n - 1)


def _et(ts):
    """(session key, minutes past ET midnight) for a UTC ISO stamp."""
    s = str(ts)
    y = int(s[0:4])
    mo = int(s[5:7])
    d = int(s[8:10])
    hh = int(s[11:13])
    mm = int(s[14:16])
    if 3 < mo < 11:
        dst = True
    elif mo == 3:
        dst = d >= _nth_sunday(y, 3, 2)
    elif mo == 11:
        dst = d < _nth_sunday(y, 11, 1)
    else:
        dst = False
    t = hh * 60 + mm - (4 if dst else 5) * 60
    return (s[:10], t) if t >= 0 else (s[:10], t + 1440)


def family_init(ctx):
    import math
    import bisect
    bars = ctx.bars
    n = len(bars)
    c = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]
    v = [float(b.get("v") or 0.0) for b in bars]

    mins = [0] * n
    for t in range(n):
        mins[t] = _et(bars[t]["t"])[1]
    ctx.mins = mins

    # The construction lives entirely inside the regular session. An
    # extended-hours bar carries a few hundred shares against a few hundred
    # thousand in the session, and mixing them makes the bucket size
    # meaningless in both directions at once.
    reg = [t for t in range(n) if 570 <= mins[t] < 960]
    pos = {}
    for k, t in enumerate(reg):
        pos[t] = k
    m = len(reg)
    ctx.pos = pos

    rc = [float(c[reg[k]]) for k in range(m)]
    rv = [float(v[reg[k]]) for k in range(m)]

    # ---- clock-time squared returns, prefix-summed ----
    csq = [0.0] * (m + 1)
    for k in range(1, m):
        a, b = rc[k - 1], rc[k]
        x = math.log(b / a) if (a > 0.0 and b > 0.0) else 0.0
        csq[k + 1] = csq[k] + x * x

    # ---- volume clock: equal-volume buckets, V refreshed causally ----
    mw = int(ctx.p.med_win)
    step = max(1, int(ctx.p.re_n))
    bclose = []
    bat = []                      # the regular-bar index each bucket closed on
    acc = 0.0
    V = None
    for k in range(m):
        if k >= mw and (V is None or k % step == 0):
            w = sorted(rv[k - mw:k])
            mid = w[len(w) // 2]
            V = mid if mid > 0.0 else None
        if V is None:
            continue
        prev = rc[k - 1] if k > 0 else rc[k]
        vol = rv[k]
        used = 0.0
        guard = 0
        while vol - used > 1e-9 and guard < 200:
            guard += 1
            need = V - acc
            if vol - used >= need:
                used += need
                acc = 0.0
                f = used / vol if vol > 0.0 else 1.0
                bclose.append(prev + (rc[k] - prev) * f)
                bat.append(k)
            else:
                acc += vol - used
                used = vol
    nb = len(bclose)
    vsq = [0.0] * (nb + 1)
    for j in range(1, nb):
        a, b = bclose[j - 1], bclose[j]
        x = math.log(b / a) if (a > 0.0 and b > 0.0) else 0.0
        vsq[j + 1] = vsq[j] + x * x

    # buckets completed as of each regular bar
    done = [0] * m
    j = 0
    for k in range(m):
        while j < nb and bat[j] <= k:
            j += 1
        done[k] = j

    # ---- Q = RV_clock / RV_vol, and its trailing percentile rank ----
    W = int(ctx.p.rv_win)
    pw = int(ctx.p.pct_win)
    Q = [None] * m
    for k in range(W, m):
        K = done[k]
        if K < W + 1:
            continue
        a = csq[k + 1] - csq[k + 1 - W]
        b = vsq[K] - vsq[K - W]
        if a > 0.0 and b > 1e-16:
            Q[k] = a / b

    pct = [None] * n
    hist = []                     # the trailing window, kept sorted
    fifo = []                     # the same values in arrival order
    head = 0
    for k in range(m):
        q = Q[k]
        if q is None:
            continue
        if len(hist) >= int(ctx.p.pct_min):
            lo = bisect.bisect_left(hist, q)
            hi = bisect.bisect_right(hist, q)
            pct[reg[k]] = (lo + hi) * 0.5 / len(hist)
        bisect.insort(hist, q)
        fifo.append(q)
        if len(hist) > pw:
            old = fifo[head]
            head += 1
            j = bisect.bisect_left(hist, old)
            if j < len(hist) and hist[j] == old:
                hist.pop(j)
    ctx.pct = pct

    ctx.rk = [None] * n           # regular-session index, for the r30 lookback
    for k, t in enumerate(reg):
        ctx.rk[t] = k
    ctx.rc = rc
    ctx.start = mw + W + int(ctx.p.pct_min) + 2


def signal(ctx, i):
    k = ctx.rk[i]
    if k is None or k < ctx.start:
        return 0
    mi = ctx.mins[i]
    if mi < int(ctx.p.t_open) or mi > int(ctx.p.t_close):
        return 0
    p = ctx.pct[i]
    if p is None or p < float(ctx.p.pct_in):
        return 0
    look = int(ctx.p.look)
    if k - look < 0:
        return 0
    a = ctx.rc[k - look]
    b = ctx.rc[k]
    if a <= 0.0 or b <= 0.0 or a == b:
        return 0
    # price has moved far per unit of clock time and little per unit of
    # volume: the move is unbacked by participation, so fade it
    return -1 if b > a else 1


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    p = ctx.pct[i]
    if p is None:
        return False
    return p < float(ctx.p.pct_out)
